one-check-per-line.why: all 6 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 6

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 6 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why: I compared each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Checks 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 mostly stay within those words. Check 4 does not. Expect line 4 says only "lint(text) in src/index.js is unchanged", but Check 4 fails the PR on "any diff in packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js", which it tests with `git diff --exit-code <base sha> HEAD -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js`. That is a file-scope rule: an edit elsewhere in the file that leaves lint(text) alone would fail. Check 4 also makes `node --test packages/jsonl-lint/test/lint.test.js` passing a PASS condition, which is a test the words don't require. The criterion says such stricter rules belong under Advisory, but here they are pass/fail conditions.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs against the 15 tracked files and the scripts. They all point to things that exist: bin/jsonl-lint.js, src/index.js, test/cli.test.js, test/lint.test.js, the README, and `npm test` at the root, which runs the workspace `node --test`. The verifier's shell is valid. The fixture `printf` lines, `{ ...; } > "$T/single.txt"`, `diff`, `node $B - - < "$T/a.jsonl"`, and `node --test packages/jsonl-lint/test/lint.test.js` all run from the root. The jq filters (`select(.body // "" | contains("issues/104"))`, `@tsv`) are valid, and the `gh api` REST paths are real endpoints. Placeholders like `<PR number>` and `<base sha>` come from earlier commands. The builder's sanity command also runs as written. One weak spot: package.json is probably multi-line JSON, so that command would likely print package.json errors too, not only `-:1:`. That is wrong expected output, not a command that fails, so the criterion still holds.

catches-traps.why:
The briefs handle all four must_catch items.
(1) Verifier Check 3 runs `"$T/a.jsonl" "$T/missing.jsonl" "$T/c.jsonl"`, where c.jsonl holds the bad row `nope`. It requires exit 2, an error on stderr naming missing.jsonl, and `$T/c.jsonl:1: ...` still printed on stdout. So it tests the missing file and the bad row together, not each alone.
(2) Check 4 gets the PR's base sha with gh api and runs `git diff --exit-code <base sha> HEAD -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js`. It passes only if the diff is empty.
(3) Builder step 5 tells the builder to update packages/jsonl-lint/README.md with the multi-file usage, the `-` stdin form and the exit codes.
(4) Check 6 reads the PR body through gh api and requires it to contain the Closes line. It also requires the `test` check run at the head sha to be completed with conclusion success.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked every verifier PASS/FAIL condition against its expect line. Checks 1–3 cover the behaviour lines and each one runs the CLI (`node $B ...`, piped stdin, exit codes, a stdout diff against single-file runs); none passes a behaviour line by reading the code alone. Their conditions only test what the lines say: the `<file>:<line>: <error>` format, file order, `-` naming, exit codes 0/1/2, and that stderr has "a message" with no exact wording. Check 4 (empty diff of index.js) and Check 5 (reading the tests and README) read files, but they cover lines 4–5, not lines 1–3. Check 6 requires one PR, the Closes text and green checks, which is no stricter than line 6. Neither brief adds a branch-name rule or a mutation test. The builder's suggested stderr text ("jsonl-lint: cannot read") is guidance, not a check. Changes outside the package are only advisory ("not pass/fail"), so no file-scope limit is enforced.

methods-private.why:
I compared the builder brief's steps with the verifier's checks. Mostly the builder brief restates expect lines and asks for tests, which is allowed. It breaks the criterion in two places where it hands over the verifier's own probes:

1. Step 6 gives a hand probe with its expected output: `printf '{bad}\n' | node ... jsonl-lint.js packages/jsonl-lint/package.json -` "(expect `-:1: ...`, exit 1)". This is close to Verifier Check 2's third run (`printf '{bad}\n' | node $B "$T/a.jsonl" - ...`, PASS on `-:1: ...`, exit 1). The command is the builder's own, not one named by an expect line or the issue.
2. Step 4 says to "put a bad file after the missing one and assert its rows are still printed". This copies Check 3's PASS condition for the last run (missing.jsonl then c.jsonl, c.jsonl still reported). The expect lines don't ask for that case.

Step 3's "git diff for that file must be empty" also echoes Check 4's PASS condition.
